question: Find the volume of the largest right circular cone that can be cut out from a cube whose edge is 3(1)/(2) cm, correct to two places of decimals (use π = (22)/(7)).
solution:
**Given ; **

Edge of cube = 3frac12 cm

**Formula used :**

The volume of the cone (V) = frac13πr²h

**Concept used :**

Here, the height and the diameter are the same as the edge because the cone will have the same measurement all over its surface as the edge.

**Calculation :**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/8b7bb8a6cfc606d47dfa3fe4dd489ec4f28fbd8a0fd16d625e497e904c053de4.png] 

Edge of cone = 3frac12 cm = 7/2

The radius of cone = 7/4

Height of cone = 3frac12

⇒ Volume = (1/3)π( 7/4)²(7/2)

⇒ V = (1/3)π( 7/4)2(7/2)

⇒ V = (1/3)π( 7/4)2(7/2) = (22 × 7³) / (3 × 7× 32)

⇒ V = 7,546 / 672 = 11.229 cm³

**Hence, the correct option (3).**
